description.en: Orchestrator-preset workflows in format 2. The shipped workflow-orchestrator preset (only it can see the creation/start tools) turns a one-off request into a node graph and runs it: each robot keeps one session for the whole run in its workspace under the normal worker preset, compacting that session's history before every later entry; gate nodes pause on the normal approval dialog; gate-free runs return the run id as soon as the first node is dispatched and a host-side supervisor keeps scheduling sessions from session events (it never awaits the session result). Robots are normal sessions (runtime roots under the normal approval policy): they can request tool approvals or ask the user questions, and the run page shows a pending-interaction notice with an open-session action; the workflow injects only the task, the declared result contract and the path meanings. Every robot node session also gets four read-only observation tools available when its recorded session id belongs to a run: buka_workflow_overview (compact graph, node summaries/states and the ordered execution list without prompts or final texts), buka_workflow_execution_input and buka_workflow_execution_output (one execution's exact input or recorded output plus its attachment manifest), and buka_workflow_execution_attachment (list or read one attachment in bounded chunks). Attachments are a built-in capability of every robot node for independent data/files (binaries, archives, traces, large datasets), not a channel for the answer itself: a node may return an optional attachments array of workspace-relative paths, the observer copies those files into the execution's node directory, and later prompts can inline small text files or reference them by path. Visibility is rebuilt from run records, so the tools remain available after the run ends or DSH restarts when the robot session is reopened. Releasing a node's live agent re-announces its still-persisted session to clients, so it stays in the sidebar and the page's open-session action keeps working (it refreshes a stale client session list first). Every robot node must declare output, a JSON Schema object for its result JSON; the engine merges next and the built-in attachments capability into the scoped structured_output tool (plain-text JSON is accepted and validated the same way) and validates edge-prompt template variables against the declared schemas at plan time. When the node has outgoing edges, the JSON must carry next with one of those edge names; the supervisor follows that edge and its prompt automatically - no when condition and no extra judge agent. A terminal robot node still returns JSON but no next. Edges are { to, name, prompt }: name is the unique route key, prompt explains that entry's task and what each next value means; report and when are validation errors. There is no default node timeout (an explicit robot timeoutMs is the only hard deadline), interrupted sessions are resumed in the same session; if that fails the run fails with an explicit error and never opens a substitute session, and unfinished runs resume after a host restart except gate runs waiting for approval. Runs are one-off and format 2 only: on startup old-version runs are purged, run numbering restarts at #1 and settings.json keeps the archive settings. A read-only sidebar page draws each persisted run as a vertical git-like graph of capsules with nested side lanes that never cross, mid-path arrows, ×N revisits and gray unreached nodes; robot capsules show the robot's preset avatar and the creator-written step summary, the detail panel shows the node's single robot session with an open-session action, and one tab per execution shows the rendered task, the final text, status, time, duration and the route it took, plus a pending-interaction notice and recovered/timed-out tags; the output tab shows the final text and attachment downloads, never the raw JSON or key/value routing fields. Every run is numbered in creation order (#N); the page's auto-archive settings archive runs after 24 hours and delete them after 168 hours by default.
description.zh-cn: 由编排 preset 创建的一次性工作流（格式 2）：随插件发布的 workflow-orchestrator preset 是唯一能看到创建类工具入口的 preset，它把一次性需求变成节点图并启动；同一个机器人在一次运行里共用一个会话，首次进入时新开、之后每次进入都先 compact 压缩历史再把新的边 prompt 发进同一会话（普通工作 preset）；门禁节点弹原生审批框；不含门禁的运行在第一个节点 dispatch 后工具就返回，由宿主侧观察者订阅会话事件继续调度（不 await 会话结果）。机器人是普通会话（运行时根会话、正常审批策略）：可以在会话里请求工具审批或向用户提问，运行页会提示等待交互并可直接打开会话；工作流只提供任务、输出契约与路径含义，不注入行为提示词。每个机器人节点会话还会获得四个只读观测工具（按运行记录里的 sessionId 判定可见性）：buka_workflow_overview 返回紧凑节点图、节点概要 / 状态与按顺序排列的执行列表，不返回 prompt 或最终文本；buka_workflow_execution_input 与 buka_workflow_execution_output 按执行序号读取某次执行的输入、输出与附件清单；buka_workflow_execution_attachment 列出附件或分段读取其中一个大文本。附件是每个机器人节点的内置能力，用来交回与答案相互独立的文件 / 数据（二进制、压缩包、trace、大数据集），不是答案本身；机器人节点可返回可选的 attachments（工作区相对路径数组），观察者把文件复制到该次执行的节点目录；后续 prompt 可以内联小文本附件，也可以只引用路径。可见性会从运行记录重建，运行结束或 DSH 重启后重新打开机器人会话时工具仍然可用。节点结束释放 live agent 时会把仍持久化的会话重新通告给客户端，所以它不会从侧边栏消失，运行页「打开会话」照常可用（客户端列表缺这条会话时会先刷新一次）。每个机器人节点都必须声明 output（结果 JSON 的 JSON Schema）；引擎把 output、next 与内置附件能力合并后装到 scoped 工具 structured_output 上（纯文本 JSON 也接受，并且同样校验），并在计划阶段按声明的 schema 校验边 prompt 里的模板变量；节点有出边时 JSON 必须带 next，值为某条出边的 name，观察者照这条边（连同 prompt）自动前进，没有 when 条件也不需要额外的判断 agent；终止机器人节点仍交回 JSON 但不用 next。边是 { to, name, prompt }：name 是该节点内唯一的路由键，prompt 写清这次进入的任务与每个 next 值的含义；report / when 是校验错误。默认不设节点超时（只有显式 timeoutMs 才是硬截止）；会话中断只续接同一会话，续接失败直接终止运行并写明原因，不会新开替代会话；DSH 重启后未完成的运行继续跑（等待审批的门禁运行除外）。运行一次性且只支持格式 2：启动时清理旧版本运行、编号从 #1 重新开始，settings.json（自动归档设置）保留。侧边栏「工作流」页面只负责观测：把每次运行画成类似 git log 的纵向节点图（跨行 / 循环边走右侧竖线 lane、内层靠里外层包在外面不交叉，每条连线带中段箭头，重复进入标 ×N，未走到的节点灰色虚线）；机器人胶囊显示头像与创建者写的步骤概要，详情只展示该节点的一个会话并可「打开会话」，按「第几次执行」的 Tab 查看那次的任务、最终文本、状态 / 时间 / 时长与走出的 route，恢复过 / 超时或等待用户时都有提示；输出展示最终文本与附件下载入口，不铺路由字段、也不展示原始 JSON。每次运行按创建顺序编号 #N；页面「归档设置」默认超过 24 小时归档、超过 168 小时删除。
